candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture fits SC-PMVT/VF: collapse at rest, short-coupling interval of 240 ms, monomorphic PVCs with atypical LBBB/left-axis morphology triggering polymorphic VT/VF, normal echo, normal coronaries, and normal electrolytes. CPVT classically requires adrenergic provocation (exercise/catecholamines) and typically shows bidirectional or polymorphic VT during stress testing, not short-coupled PVCs at rest. Although a RyR2 variant is present, it is of unknown significance and RyR2 variants are also described in SC-PMVT/VF; the candidate incorrectly assigns the CPVT diagnosis based on the RyR2 finding alone, conflicting with the established SC-PMVT/VF subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: CPVT is a distinct arrhythmia syndrome triggered by adrenergic stress, whereas SC-PMVT/VF is a separate idiopathic VF variant characterized by short-coupled PVCs at rest triggering polymorphic VT/VF without structural heart disease or adrenergic dependence

case_quality_flags: RyR2 variant of unknown significance noted in SC-PMVT/VF context — overlapping genetic substrate does not equate to CPVT diagnosis
No exercise stress test result documented, but resting short-coupling interval and absence of adrenergic trigger strongly favor SC-PMVT/VF over CPVT
